I am 55 years old and have farmed in Quzhou County for 30 years. I finished middle school. My family has 16.9 mu of land. There are three of us in the household, but my son and daughter-in-law both work at a factory in the county town, so most days I am the one in the fields. I have a well, so when the rain does not come, I can irrigate.

Last year I planted 11 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 5.9 mu in cotton. This year I will do exactly the same. I do not change my cropping plan from a blank slate — last year the harvest was decent, so why take risks? My neighbor Lao Wang has a similar-sized farm and he uses about the same amounts. If he does well, I copy him. That is how I have always done it.

For winter wheat, I sow in early October with an improved variety — last year I used Liangxing 77 and it gave me about 960 jin per mu. This year I will sow about 30 jin of seed per mu. Before sowing I do rotary tillage to break up the soil. At sowing I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 50 kg of 18-22-5. Then at green-up time in March I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. In total that works out to about 17 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings from freezing, once at jointing stage around April, and once at grain filling in May. I spray twice — once with herbicide right after sowing, and once with insecticide if I see aphids. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather is normal. I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money.

For summer maize, I plant immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I do not till — I use a no-tillage seeder because there is no time to waste between harvest and sowing. I use hybrid seed, Nongda 372 or something similar from the dealer, about 1.5 kg per mu. At sowing I apply 50 kg of 28-6-6 compound fertilizer per mu, which gives me about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium. If the plants look yellow at the big trumpet stage, I might spread a little more urea, but usually the basal is enough. I irrigate twice — once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at tasseling in August. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for corn borer. I expect about 580 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plant 5.9 mu in late April. Cotton is labor-intensive, which is why I only keep 5.9 mu of it — with my son and daughter-in-law away at work, I cannot manage more by myself. I use hybrid cotton seed, about 2 jin per mu. I do rotary tillage in spring. I put down 60 kg of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and topdress twice with urea during the season. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs water at budding, flowering, and boll stage, so I irrigate three times. The biggest headache is pests. I spray 5 times — for aphids early on, red spider mite, and especially cotton bollworm. Bollworm can destroy everything if you are lazy. I expect about 300 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I think about costs carefully. A bag of urea is about 100 yuan now, compound fertilizer is more. Every yuan counts. But if I cut back too much, I lose yield, and that is worse. Wheat and maize prices are steady around 1.1 to 1.2 yuan per jin, cotton was about 6 yuan per kg last year. With 16.9 mu I am not the biggest farmer around, but I am not the smallest either. I can absorb a small risk, but I still watch every input. I do most labor myself, but at wheat and maize harvest I hire a combine — it is faster and my back is not what it used to be.
